outcome_assessed: Psychological well-being (Adapted Ryff scale, AVRPWB, self-report, brailled); post-test week 14; EI training and LOC training arms each vs conventional-method control
support_D1: Three purposively selected schools 'assigned to treatment groups through the use of ballot system' (Ch3 3.5), so sequence plausibly random, but only one school per arm; concealment not described; design labelled 'true-experimental' (Ch3 3.1) and 'quasi experimental' (Abstract); pre-test means not reported (Ch4); arm composition differs markedly (females 8 EI, 15 LOC, 5 control; Ch3 Table 1). Ballot of schools counts as plausibly random cluster allocation under the guide (RoB 2 cluster even with one cluster per arm).
support_D1b: Participants were the visually impaired pupils of each school, 40 'purposively selected' per school (Ch3 3.4, 3.6); inclusion required 'willingness to participate in the treatment programme when first introduced by the head of school' (Ch3 3.5); Table 4 places 'assigning the students to treatment groups' in week 1 with pre-test in weeks 2-3, so pupils were identified/consented after allocation was known, with no blinding of recruiters reported.
support_D2: Pupils and deliverers (class teachers trained as research assistants; Ch3 3.8.2-3.8.3) aware of allocation; control met only at pre and post (Ch3 Table 4 note); fidelity monitored weekly by researcher (3.8.3); no deviations reported; all 120 analysed by group (Ch4 Table 5-6). Session length inconsistent (1 h vs 2 h).
support_D3: All 120 allocated appear analysed: ANCOVA total df 119 and N=40 per arm (Ch4 Tables 5-6); no attrition reported.
support_D4: Self-reported well-being by pupils who knew they received training; class teachers assisted with brailled materials (3.8.1); assessor blinding not reported. Instrument item count inconsistent (25 vs 20 items; 3.7.2, 3.7.5).
support_D5: No protocol or registration; single outcome analysed by pre-specified ANCOVA (Ch3, Ch4 Table 5), but pre-test means not reported and reported values inconsistent between text and tables (Ch4 Tables 5-7).
unit_of_analysis_note: Schools allocated (1 per arm, 3 arms) but pupils analysed by ANCOVA without accounting for clustering; treatment fully confounded with school (Ch3 Table 1; Ch4 Table 5).
integrity_note: LOC adjusted mean 75.07 (Ch4 text) vs 74.07 (Table 7); three-way interaction F=0.813 with P=0.833 (Table 5) while MS 29.988/163.673 gives F=0.183; total MS printed '219,797'; abstract subgroup means differ from Ch4 text; AVRPWB 25 vs 20 items; session 1 h vs 2 h; text under Hypothesis 5 concludes 'hypothesis four is accepted'.
reconciliation_notes: Tool differed (x1 RoB 2 cluster; x2 ROBINS-I V2), so all domain ratings and overall (High vs Serious) differed. Ch3 3.5 states 'The schools were assigned to treatment groups through the use of ballot system'; schools were the allocation unit, so the guide requires RoB 2 for cluster-randomised trials even with one school per arm. Adopted x1 domain ratings after re-reading Ch3 3.4-3.6 and Table 4 (allocation in week 1, pre-test weeks 2-3, 40 purposively selected per school with willingness criterion): D1 Some concerns, D1b Some concerns (recruitment after allocation, no baseline means to show imbalance), D2 Some concerns, D3 Low (120 analysed), D4 Some concerns, D5 Some concerns. Overall High: five of six domains Some concerns with treatment fully confounded with school, which substantially lowers confidence.

outcome_assessed: Depressive symptoms (Goldberg depression scale, 18 items, self-report); post-test (Time 2)
support_D1: Simple random allocation sequence by software (Saghaei) with allocation 'concealed' from participants and research assistants (Participants/procedure section) and no pretest group difference F(1,73)=.381, P=.539 (Results), so sequence and concealment adequate; but 37/37 randomised (Abstract; procedure) vs Table 1 n=32 treatment/42 control and significant pretest Group x Gender interaction F=18.077, p<.001 (Table 1) raise unexplained concerns about the randomised groups.
support_D2: Participants and therapist aware of allocation; comparator described as conventional counselling 12 x 1 h (2.1), 'waitlisted control' (Abstract) and 'no-contact control' (2.5, Results), so what the control received is unclear; refreshments given to attendees; analysis by randomised group cannot be confirmed (32/42 vs 37/37).
support_D3: Authors state no absences and full completion (2.1), and post-test F df (1,73) suggests ~74 analysed, but per-arm Ns in Table 1 contradict allocation; later-test df (1,56) implies missing data at follow-up (not the time point assessed).
support_D4: Self-reported depression by children aware of receiving REBT; no assessor blinding reported; post-test timing ambiguous ('after 2 months of completing the study', 2.1).
support_D5: No protocol or trial registration; single scale with total and sex-specific means reported (Table 1); multivariate/ANCOVA approach loosely described (2.5).
unit_of_analysis_note: Individual allocation within 7 special schools; no clustering issue for allocation, but sessions delivered in groups and school clustering not considered.
integrity_note: Randomised 37/37 but Table 1 n=32/42; state given as Abia (2.1) and Enugu (Abstract, Discussion); randomisation software reference [35] does not match; control means essentially unchanged and later-test values duplicate pretest/post-test values (Table 1); later-test df (1,56) vs (1,73) with N=74; significant pretest Group x Gender interaction.
reconciliation_notes: D1 differed (x1 High; x2 Some concerns). Re-read procedure and Table 1: sequence generation (software) and concealment are stated, and pretest groups did not differ (F(1,73)=.381); under the RoB 2 algorithm High needs inadequate sequence/concealment or baseline imbalance with unclear concealment, so final Some concerns, with the 37/37 vs 32/42 mismatch carried in D2, D3 and integrity_note. All other domains agreed (all Some concerns). Overall High agreed: all five domains Some concerns with unexplained group-size discrepancy substantially lower confidence.

outcome_assessed: PTSD symptoms, total score (adapted UCLA PTSD Reaction Index, 20 items, self-report); post-test after 6-week programme (subscales re-experiencing, hyper-arousal, avoidance also reported)
support_D1: 40 SS1 students 'systematically selected and randomly assigned' 20/20; 'randomization procedure involved assigning ... without involving any potential biases or judgements' (Sample) - method of sequence generation and concealment not described; pre-test administered for eligibility but baseline scores not reported (Participants and Procedures), so baseline balance cannot be checked.
support_D2: Attention placebo (Learning Modalities, 12 x 40 min) run concurrently by research assistants; groups held in separate classrooms to limit contamination; delivery supervised against manual (Treatment/Intervention Procedure). Participants likely aware but no deviations reported; all 40 analysed by group (t-tests df 38, Tables 1-3).
support_D3: All 40 randomised analysed (t df 38; Tables 1-3; Abstract total t(38)).
support_D4: Self-report PTSD symptoms by students who received psycho-education delivered by the researcher; assessor or participant blinding not reported (Measures; Treatment).
support_D5: No protocol or registration; total score reported only in Abstract, subscales in Results Tables 1-3; post-test-only t-tests without baseline adjustment although pre-test collected; pretest data not reported.
unit_of_analysis_note: Individually allocated within school(s) (number of schools NR; Abstract says students drawn from secondary schools clustered in the conflict community); no clustering issue for allocation.
integrity_note: Pretest scores not reported; hyper-arousal control SE 2.228 (text) vs 1.228 (Table 2); minor text-table discrepancies (SD 4.10 vs 4.097; t -4.830 vs -4.829); SS1 in Methods vs SSII in conclusion; 'SPSS version 2.0'.
reconciliation_notes: D2 differed (x1 Low; x2 Some concerns). Re-read Treatment/Intervention Procedure: attention placebo (Learning Modalities, 12 x 40 min) run concurrently, 'strictly supervised by the researcher to ensure proper compliance to the rules as stipulated in the manual'; no deviations arising from the trial context reported and all 40 analysed by group (t df 38). Awareness alone does not make D2 Some concerns, so final Low. Other domains agreed. Overall Some concerns agreed (three Some concerns, no High).

outcome_assessed: Physics test anxiety (Generalized Test Anxiety Inventory, GTAI, self-report); post-test 1 week after last session (Time 2)
support_D1: 83 eligible students randomly assigned (43 E, 40 C) by each participant picking 1 envelope labelled E or C from a container; demographic information concealed from the person randomising (Methods 2.5); no baseline difference on GTAI, F(1,80)=0.753 (Results).
support_D2: Group CBT-music (12 x 90 min) vs no-intervention control; claim that participants were blinded (2.5) is implausible for this comparison; deviations and adherence not reported; df (1,80) suggests not all 83 analysed, so analysis by assignment unclear.
support_D3: Attrition not reported in text (CONSORT Fig 1 not available in text); between-group df (1,80) implies about 82 analysed and interaction df (2,76) implies fewer; reasons for any loss not given.
support_D4: Self-reported test anxiety by students who knew they received an active group programme vs nothing; stated blinding of participants/assistants (2.5) not credible.
support_D5: No registration or protocol; results reported only as F, p, eta2 and adjusted R2 with no means or SDs (Results; Table 2 not in text); GTAI scoring after reduction to 45 items unclear (2.4.1).
unit_of_analysis_note: Individually randomised; pupils from several sampled schools (number NR); group delivery, no clustering considered.
integrity_note: Baseline F(1,80)=0.753 with P=.513 is not consistent; eta2 .904 and adjusted R2 .956 mismatched; df (1,80) and (2,76) inconsistent with N=83; GTAI reduced to 45 items but range 48-240 retained; ethics ID dated 2019 vs fieldwork 2018; unrelated IEEE references (refs 27-34); means/SDs not reported in text.
reconciliation_notes: All domains agreed (D1 Low; D2-D5 Some concerns); overall differed (x1 High; x2 Some concerns). Applying the overall rule strictly: four of five domains Some concerns, with an implausible blinding claim (Methods 2.5), numbers analysed unverifiable (df (1,80) and (2,76) vs N=83), and no means or SDs reported for the outcome (Results), which together substantially lower confidence, so final High.

outcome_assessed: Aggression (Teacher Report Form, TRF, teacher-rated; score analysed unspecified); immediate post-intervention
support_D1: Called 'quasi-experimental ... non-randomized' design (Research design) but Group Allocation says the 120 pupils were 'randomly assigned' 60/60 with no method or concealment described; baseline imbalance on TRF pretest (52.78 vs 56.22, SD ~5-6; Table 1); description contradictory.
support_D2: Counsellor-led group sessions with teachers reinforcing behaviour in class and receiving weekly summaries (Intervention); intervention and control pupils from the same six schools, so contamination via teachers possible; control 'regular classroom activities'; no adherence data.
support_D3: ANCOVA residual df 115 consistent with all 120 analysed (Table 2); one row excluded for missing group (Table 1 note).
support_D4: Outcome rated by teachers who were trained to support the intervention and received weekly session summaries (Intervention; Data Collection Process), so assessors knew allocation and were involved in delivery.
support_D5: No protocol or registration; three TRF aggression-related subscales (Aggressive Behavior, Rule-Breaking, Social Problems) and three social-behaviour subscales selected (Instruments), but a single unlabelled 'TRF' score is reported (Tables 1-2); social-behaviour results and the planned 3-month follow-up (Data Collection Process) not reported; result likely selected from multiple eligible measurements.
unit_of_analysis_note: Stated individual allocation across six primary schools; clustering by school not accounted for in ANCOVA (Table 2).
integrity_note: Called quasi-experimental yet random assignment stated; TRF described as 33 items (standard TRF longer); gender effect and interaction reported without gender-specific means; follow-up stated but not reported; keyword 'Parental perceptions' unrelated.
reconciliation_notes: D3 differed (x1 Low; x2 Some concerns): ANCOVA residual df 115 with four terms implies N=120 analysed (Table 2); the 'excluded 1 row' note refers to a missing group label in the output, so Low. D4 differed (x1 High; x2 Some concerns): TRF rated by teachers trained to reinforce the intervention and given weekly session summaries (Intervention section), so assessors knew allocation and were involved in delivery; final High. D5 differed (x1 Some concerns; x2 High): multiple TRF subscales selected but one unspecified score reported, other outcomes and follow-up unreported; final High. D1 High agreed (called quasi-experimental non-randomised yet 'randomly assigned', no method; baseline imbalance 52.78 vs 56.22). Overall High agreed (D1, D4, D5 High).

outcome_assessed: Test anxiety (Adolescent Students' Test Anxiety Scale, ASTAS, researcher-developed, self-report); post-test week 8
support_D1: Despite 'randomly assigned' (Abstract; Methodology 2.0), 'subjects in one school were assigned to the experimental group, while those in second school were assigned to the control group' (2.0): one school per arm, method of school assignment NR; pretest means similar (41.5 vs 42.4; Table 2) but analysis is post-test t-test with no adjustment (Table 3).
support_D2: Intervention status defined by school at start; testwiseness package vs 'placebo' conventional talk-and-chalk (2.0, 2.3) clearly distinguished.
support_D3: 160 of 250 screened met high-anxiety/non-testwise criteria; 120 (30 M, 30 F per school) chosen from them with selection method not stated (2.3); selection based on pre-intervention characteristics, so moderate concern only.
support_D4: No information on adherence or fidelity; duration inconsistent (6 weeks Abstract vs 8 weeks 2.3); attention 'placebo' delivered; no co-interventions reported.
support_D5: 60 per arm at pre-test and post-test (Tables 2-3); no attrition apparent.
support_D6: Researcher-developed self-report scale completed by students aware of receiving training; no blinding reported (2.1-2.3).
support_D7: No protocol; single outcome with pre and post t-tests reported (Tables 2-3); t-statistic appears small for reported means/SDs, but no evidence of selection among multiple analyses.
unit_of_analysis_note: Allocation by school (1 per arm) but pupils analysed by independent t-test; treatment confounded with school, clustering not accounted for (2.0; Table 3).
integrity_note: Labelled randomised but school-level non-random allocation; 6 vs 8 weeks; post-test t=2.95 small relative to mean difference 8.3 with SDs 8.1/7.6 and n=60 per arm (expected t about 5.8); 'P<0.05' footnote under non-significant pre-test t (Table 2).
reconciliation_notes: Tool agreed (ROBINS-I V2: one intact school per arm, 'subjects in one school were assigned to the experimental group... second school... control', Methodology 2.0). D2 classification differed (x1 Low; x2 Moderate): status defined by school at the start and testwiseness vs placebo lessons clearly distinguished, with no scope for misclassification; x2 support text itself describes clear definition, so final Low. Other domains agreed. Overall Serious agreed (D1 Serious is most severe).

outcome_assessed: Anxiety (Odebunmi Anxiety scale, self-report); post-test only after 6-week REBT (depression and stress also reported)
support_D1: 'Randomly selected and divided equally' (Abstract); 'systematic random sampling method was used to select twenty-five adolescents each into the experimental and control groups' (Method of Study) - systematic (every k-th) assignment is predictable, concealment not described; post-test-only design with no baseline data, so imbalance cannot be assessed.
support_D2: REBT twice weekly for six weeks vs no treatment (Method; Discussion); participants aware; no information on adherence, deviations or numbers analysed.
support_D3: Number analysed per group and t-test df not reported (Results); attrition not mentioned.
support_D4: Self-report anxiety scale completed by adolescents aware of receiving REBT; no assessor blinding reported; scale direction and scoring not described (Method).
support_D5: No protocol; three scales reported with t only (Results); reported means contradict stated direction of effect, preventing verification of the reported result.
unit_of_analysis_note: Individual allocation; number of schools NR; no clustering issue identifiable.
integrity_note: Anxiety experimental M=49.9 higher than control 46.4 yet called 'lower'; stress 48.2 vs 45.6 called 'lower'; depression t=0.56 with 'P<0.05' yet null accepted; experimental depression SD 6.16 identical to control anxiety SD; df and n not reported; instrument year '19991'; OCR text.
reconciliation_notes: D1 differed (x1 High; x2 Some concerns): the only allocation method given is 'systematic random sampling... to select twenty-five adolescents each into the experimental and control groups' (Method of Study), a systematic, predictable assignment with no concealment and no baseline data (post-test-only design); final High. D5 differed (x1 Some concerns; x2 High): one scale and one t-test per outcome, no evidence of selection among multiple measurements or analyses; the means contradicting the stated direction are a data integrity issue (integrity_note) and per guide do not change D5, so final Some concerns. Overall High agreed (D1 High).

outcome_assessed: Examination/test anxiety (Nigerian TAI, self-report), post-test week 7; REBT vs placebo (health talks)
support_D1: Non-randomised intact groups: test-anxious students in the Edo Central school formed the REBT group and those in Edo North the control (Method, Participants; Procedures 'Pre-test'). One school per arm, arm confounded with school and senatorial district. Pretest similar (55.56 vs 55.47, Table 2) and ANCOVA with pretest, age, gender (Table 3), but school-level confounders unaddressed.
support_D2: Arms defined by school and clearly distinct: six 45-min REBT sessions vs six health-education placebo sessions, manualised (Procedures 'Intervention'; Table 1). Misclassification unlikely.
support_D3: Same screening rule (TAI >=51) applied in both schools before grouping and before the intervention started; 160 of 739 screened selected (Procedures 'Pre-test'; Results para 1). Selection not influenced by intervention or post-start outcome.
support_D4: Delivered by two trained professional counsellors from researcher manuals (Procedures); weekly participation only 80-85% and no fidelity or co-intervention data (Procedures 'Post-test').
support_D5: Post-test 69/72 REBT and 86/88 control (Table 2); dropout 3.1% (Procedures 'Post-test'); small and balanced.
support_D6: Self-report TAI completed by students who knew whether they received anxiety-focused therapy; administered by researchers and research assistants (Procedures 'Post-test').
support_D7: No protocol or registration; single eligible outcome (TAI) analysed by one ANCOVA with pre-stated hypotheses (Data analysis; Table 3). No evidence of selection among multiple outcomes or analyses. Impossible ANCOVA df (Table 3: 2/220/239 for N=155) recorded in integrity_note.
unit_of_analysis_note: Schools (1 per arm) effectively allocated; pupils analysed individually without adjustment for clustering (Table 3); treatment fully confounded with school.
integrity_note: ANCOVA df impossible (Table 3: df 2/220/239 vs N=155); placebo pretest 55.76 (4.51) in text vs 55.47 (4.69) Table 2; N stated as 155 and 160; Table 5 footnotes cite LSD and Bonferroni.
reconciliation_notes: Domains differing: D3 (A1 Low, A2 Moderate; final Low: Selection into the study was by a single pre-intervention screening rule applied identically in both schools; start of follow-up coincides with start of intervention, so nothing supports Moderate (assessor 2 gave the same support text as assessor 1).); D7 (A1 Serious, A2 Moderate; final Moderate: D7 judges selection among multiple outcome measurements or analyses; only one outcome and one analysis are reported. The impossible df is a data-integrity problem (guide: recorded in integrity_note), not evidence of selective reporting, so Moderate (no protocol) rather than Serious.) Overall Serious by ROBINS-I most-severe rule; both assessors agreed on overall.

outcome_assessed: PTSD symptoms (International Trauma Questionnaire, Hausa, self-report), post-intervention; art and music therapy (combined treatment) vs no-intervention control
support_D1: Study called a quasi-experiment (Abstract; Methods 'Study design') yet 470 students 'randomly divided/assigned' (Abstract; Methods 'Study participants'; Fig 1 'randomizing'); no sequence generation or concealment reported. Students 'recruited from two different schools to avoid the issue of contamination' (Methods), implying arms coincide with schools. Baseline ITQ similar (Table 4 Time 1, p=.421).
support_D2: Pupils and therapists aware (no-intervention control; TV-based sessions). Fidelity monitored by two external therapists, kappa >0.8 (Fidelity treatment). Analysis excluded 41 with inadequately completed questionnaires (Fig 1), not by assignment; impact probably small.
support_D3: 429/470 analysed (control 212/235, treatment 217/235; Fig 1, Results para 1); 41 excluded for 'incorrect and redundant entries'; reasons could relate to symptom severity; no sensitivity analysis.
support_D4: Self-report ITQ completed by adolescents who knew they received therapy (Methods, Data collection procedure); outcome subjective.
support_D5: No protocol or registration; both ANCOVA and repeated-measures ANOVA described (Data collection and analysis; Table 3, Table 4); art and music arms reported separately and combined; no pre-specified analysis plan.
unit_of_analysis_note: Two schools; if arms coincide with schools, clustering ignored; analysis at pupil level (Table 4). Authors' statement that two schools were used to avoid contamination suggests school-level allocation.
integrity_note: Outcome data identical to another report (R0464): same Table 4 means/SDs at all three timepoints, same F (1.008, 452.221, 482.291) and eta2 values, but different states, arms and sample. SDs implausibly small (0.21-0.65 on ITQ). F(2,428) reported with three groups while art/music analysed n not given. Assessor 2 also noted funder unrelated to topic and strong suspicion of duplicated or fabricated data.
reconciliation_notes: Domains differing: D1 (A1 High, A2 Some concerns; final High: Guide: random allocation claimed, nothing supports it and the description is contradictory (quasi-experiment; schools used to avoid contamination). With arms probably coinciding with two schools, allocation is very likely non-random, so High rather than Some concerns; baseline similarity does not offset this.) Overall High by RoB 2 rule; both assessors agreed on overall.

outcome_assessed: Depression (adapted BDI-II, self-report), post-test week 9; DBT and IPT each vs no-treatment control
support_D1: Three schools 'randomly assigned to treatment groups' (Sample and Sampling Procedure, fifth stage; Study Procedure phase 2), method not stated, but the design is labelled quasi-experimental because randomisation was 'not feasible' (Research Design) and Phase 1 says participants were randomly assigned. One school per arm. Marked baseline imbalance among eligible pupils (control school 45M/14F vs DBT 15M/26F, Table 1 distribution of sample).
support_D1b: Pupils identified by LAS-SF screening before school allocation (stage 4 before stage 5), but only 86/127 eligible 'started the treatment' after allocation was known (Table 1 distribution), with differential uptake (DBT 33/41, IPT 23/27, control 30/59); post-allocation selection possible.
support_D2: Pupils and deliverers aware; control received nothing (Research Design). Analysis restricted to 66 completers (Table 1 distribution; Results Table 1 N=22/21/23): 20 of 86 starters excluded for not completing treatment, differentially by arm. No session content, deliverer or adherence described (Study Procedure).
support_D3: Outcome available for 66 of 127 eligible (52%) and 66 of 86 starters (Table 1 distribution); losses differ by arm (control 29/59 not started); no analysis addressing missingness.
support_D4: Adapted BDI-II self-reported by pupils aware of receiving therapy (Research Instruments; Phase 3).
support_D5: No protocol or registration; two outcomes each analysed by ANCOVA with LSD (Tables 2-3, 5-6); no evidence of choice among multiple analyses but no pre-specified plan.
unit_of_analysis_note: One school per arm allocated; pupils analysed individually by ANCOVA (Table 2) with no adjustment for clustering; treatment confounded with school.
integrity_note: BDI-II pretest means about 60 (SD about 6) near the standard maximum of 63 (Results Table 1); adapted scoring not described; intervention sessions not described. Text IPT mean 38.28 vs Table 38.24; duplicate Table 1 numbering.
reconciliation_notes: Domains differing: D2 (A1 High, A2 Some concerns; final High: Exclusion of 20/86 (23%) starters for non-completion is a failure to analyse participants in their allocated groups (RoB 2 signalling 2.6 No) with potential substantial, arm-differential impact (2.7 Yes), which the algorithm rates High; assessor 2 cited the same completers-only analysis but under-rated it.) Overall High by RoB 2 rule; both assessors agreed on overall.

outcome_assessed: Anxiety severity (SMGAD-C, labelled 'SMSAD', first-listed scale; self-report), post-test Time 2 after 12 weeks; MTCBP vs waitlist
support_D1: Simple random allocation sequence using Random Allocation Software (Saghaei); allocation concealed from therapists and participants (3.4 Procedure). Baseline groups similar on demographics (Table 1 text) and all three scales (Results para 1).
support_D2: Waitlist control; participants and therapists necessarily aware of the music/CBT sessions (3.4-3.5); flow diagram (Fig 1) and Table 3 not in the available text, so deviations and analysed numbers cannot be verified; repeated-measures ANOVA df (1,154) suggests all 155 analysed.
support_D3: Attrition not reported; Fig 1 and Table 3 (means, SDs, n) unavailable in the text; F(1,154) consistent with complete data but cannot be confirmed (Results).
support_D4: Self-report SMGAD-C completed by adolescents aware of receiving the intervention (3.1, 3.4); data analysts blinded (3.4) does not address outcome assessor.
support_D5: Registered only after completion (UMIN000035508; Ethics statement). Three anxiety scales and several analyses (RM-ANOVA, Mann-Whitney, one-sample and paired t-tests) with no pre-specified primary analysis (3.6 Statistical analysis; Results). All three scales are reported for the same comparisons, so selection among them is not evident. Retraction and impossible statistics recorded in integrity_note.
unit_of_analysis_note: Individually randomised; number of schools NR and nesting acknowledged but not modelled (5.1 Limitations); group delivery not accounted.
integrity_note: RETRACTED ARTICLE. Table 1 states participants in university, colleges of education, secondary and primary schools, contradicting the secondary-school sample; follow-up timing 6 months (3.4) vs 3 months (Abstract, Results); paired t df 154 for treatment group of 78; extremely large F (4708.364, eta2 0.968). Implausible t(77)=176.675; Tables 1 and 3 missing from available text.
reconciliation_notes: Domains differing: D5 (A1 High, A2 Some concerns; final Some concerns: Post-hoc registration and multiple analyses give Some concerns, but all three scales and all analyses are reported, so there is no evidence that the reported result was selected (RoB 2 5.2/5.3 not PY). Retraction and impossible df are integrity issues recorded in integrity_note; overall remains High via several Some concerns plus integrity.) Overall High by RoB 2 rule; both assessors agreed on overall. Overall High because four domains are Some concerns (D2-D5) in a retracted report with impossible statistics, which substantially lowers confidence.

outcome_assessed: Teacher-rated aggressive behaviour (TRAB total), post-intervention (1 week); problem-solving group intervention vs waitlist
support_D1: Two schools 'with similar profiles' were 'randomly allocated' to intervention or wait-list (Methods, Study design); method and concealment not reported; one school per arm. Baseline demographics similar (Table 1); baseline TRAB 29.6 vs 32.4 (Tables 2-3) but SRAS and ATAQ differ.
support_D1b: Pupils identified after school allocation: class teachers rated all consenting boys on TRAB and the top 20 per school were recruited (Study procedure); teachers' knowledge of allocation could have influenced selection; baseline characteristics similar (Table 1).
support_D2: Waitlist control; pupils and deliverer aware, but manualised 6-session programme delivered by a clinical psychologist with on-site supervision by the first author, as planned (Methods 'Intervention'; Study procedure). Teachers observed sessions as a planned element and did not participate (Study procedure). No deviations arising from the trial context reported; 37/40 analysed in allocated groups, 3 dropouts (Tables 2-3), unlikely to have substantial impact.
support_D3: 3/40 lost (2 intervention, 1 control; Table 2-3 notes); 92.5% with outcome data, balanced.
support_D4: TRAB completed by class teachers who knew their school's allocation; intervention-school teachers observed sessions and were briefed by researchers (Study procedure; Impact on teachers). Authors note possible socially desirable responding (Limitations). Rater knowledge likely influenced subjective ratings.
support_D5: No registration; authors mention a study protocol (Authors' contributions) but it is not available; many outcomes (TRAB, SDQ subscales, SRAS, ATAQ, SCAS) with t-tests and ANCOVA; ANCOVA reported only for TRAB, SRAS and SDQ conduct (Table 5).
unit_of_analysis_note: One school per arm randomised; 37 pupils analysed individually (t-tests, ANCOVA, Tables 4-5) without clustering adjustment; treatment confounded with school.
integrity_note: Stated score ranges inconsistent with item structure (SRAS 14 items 0-2 but range 0-14; ATAQ 18 items but range 19-76; TRAB mixed 3/5-point, range 0-42); Table 4 ATAQ retaliation t 1.72 with p 0.94; SDQ conduct t -2.39 (Table 4) vs -2.37 (text); TRAB ANCOVA F(1,34) vs SRAS F(1,35). Bonferroni alpha 0.01 but p 0.02-0.03 starred; SCAS SD 5.3 vs 5.68.
reconciliation_notes: Domains differing: D2 (A1 Low, A2 Some concerns; final Low: Lack of blinding alone does not raise D2; delivery was supervised on site and followed the protocol, teacher observation was planned, and the small balanced exclusion (3/40) cannot have substantial impact, so Low; assessor 2 gave no specific deviation.) Overall High by RoB 2 rule; both assessors agreed on overall.

outcome_assessed: Psychological wellbeing (MHC-SF total, self-report), post-test after 4 sessions; psycho-education vs no training
support_D1: Pupils allocated by hat-and-draw (Participants; Procedure) - plausibly random; concealment not reported; per-arm n not given; pretest administered but no baseline data reported (Procedure, Results); Procedure also refers to 'two classes (treatment and control groups)', leaving allocation unit unclear.
support_D2: No-treatment control; participants and researchers aware. Authors report participants 'were not consistent in the four sessions' (Limitations); no attendance or adherence data.
support_D3: t-test df 46 implies 48 analysed (Table 2), but per-arm numbers and any losses are not reported.
support_D4: Self-report MHC-SF completed by students aware of receiving psycho-education (Procedure); authors note social desirability (Limitations).
support_D5: No protocol or registration; pretest collected but not reported; only an unadjusted post-test t-test presented (Method of statistical analyses; Table 2); MHC-SF subscales not reported.
unit_of_analysis_note: Individual allocation across two schools (24 per school); school not accounted; if allocation was by class (Procedure) clustering ignored.

outcome_assessed: Insomnia severity (Insomnia Severity Index 0-28, self-report; stated primary outcome); post-intervention (1 week after last session in one intervention school and both control schools, immediately after in the second intervention school); CBT-based group intervention vs waiting list (Table 3; Outcome measures)

outcome_assessed: Emotional disposition (adapted Psychological Distress Scale, self-report; lower = better); post-test at week 8 after 6-week intervention; social learning therapy and CBT each vs waiting-list control (Tables 1-3)
support_D1: 'The three schools were randomly assigned to the counselling strategies and the control group' and 'The sampled groups ... were randomly assigned' (Methodology; Phase Two), but no method of sequence generation or concealment, and the study is labelled quasi-experimental; one school per arm. Baseline 31.61, 29.00, 31.88 (Table 1). Random allocation claimed but unsupported and contradicted by the design label: rated High per guide.
support_D1b: Screening for truancy (score 130 and above) in the three selected schools is described before schools were assigned (Methodology), but the order is not stated clearly and assignment is also placed after pre-test (Phase Two); recruiters' knowledge of allocation at identification is unclear.
support_D2: Unblinded pupils and counsellors; control on waiting list (Phase Two); no fidelity or attendance information; participants 'affirmed that they had an impressive reduction' (Phase Three), indicating awareness of the intervention's aims.
support_D3: 130 pupils completed pre-test and post-test (Administration of the Treatment; Table 1).
support_D4: Self-report distress scale completed by unblinded pupils; research assistants were told the objectives of the study and administered/scored instruments (Recruitment and Training of Research Assistants).
support_D5: No protocol or registration; two outcomes reported; truancy outcome labelled 'disruptive behaviour' in Table 4 and its scale direction never stated, but for emotional disposition a single measure and ANCOVA are reported (Tables 1-2); no clear evidence of selection for this outcome.
unit_of_analysis_note: One school per arm (three schools); pupil-level ANCOVA with no adjustment for clustering (Methodology; Table 2).
integrity_note: (1) Truancy scores rose from pre to post in SLT (37.78 to 65.00) and CBT (38.84 to 54.57) while text claims reduction (Table 4). (2) Selection criterion 'scored 130 and above' inconsistent with a 25-item 4-point scale and group means 36-39. (3) Table 5 error SS and MS identical (32232.223) with df 129. (4) Very large effects (F 168.7). These mainly concern the truancy outcome, not the outcome assessed.
reconciliation_notes: Tool differed (A1 RoB 2 cluster, A2 ROBINS-I V2; final RoB 2 cluster: 'The three schools were randomly assigned to the counselling strategies and the control group' (Methodology) and 'The sampled groups ... were randomly assigned' (Phase Two), but no method is given and the design is 'quasi-experimental' (Abstract; Research Design). Guide rule for random-claimed, unsupported, contradictory allocation: RoB 2 cluster with D1 High (as R2762).) Because of the tool difference every domain and the overall differed; final domain ratings follow assessor 1 after re-reading the full text (D1 High; D1b Some concerns; D2 Some concerns; D3 Low; D4 Some concerns; D5 Some concerns). Overall High by RoB 2 rule (D1 High); assessors' overall judgements differed only by tool (High vs Serious).

outcome_assessed: Aggression and violence (adapted Buss-Perry Aggression and Violence Questionnaire, self-report; higher = more aggression implied); post-test after 4-week CBI programme; CBI vs usual advisory talk (Table 1)
support_D1: Individual allocation by coin toss: 'Participants were asked to throw coin ... one face is for treatment and the other is for control' (p.62) - a random method, though described as 'balloting with replacement' and the design is called 'non-randomized ... non-equivalent' (p.61). No concealment issue with a public coin toss, but the contradictory description and baseline difference (pretest 11.50 vs 15.17; Table 1) raise some concerns.
support_D2: Pupils and deliverers aware of allocation; control received usual advisory talk (p.62); no fidelity or attendance data; analysis population unclear (see D3).
support_D3: 44 pupils stated as the sample (Abstract; p.61) but only 22 (11 per arm) appear in the analysis (Table 1); the missing half is not explained and could depend on outcome; no sensitivity analysis.
support_D4: Self-report questionnaire by unblinded pupils; researchers told participants they intended 'to help the respondents to be cheerful to overcome their aggression' (p.62-63) and offered rewards for participation; could influence reporting.
support_D5: No protocol or registration; single outcome; conclusion of reduction contradicts reported means (treatment post-test 48.18 vs control 16.60; Table 1) and ANCOVA statistics are internally impossible, so the reported result's derivation is unclear, but no evidence of choosing among multiple measures.
unit_of_analysis_note: Individually allocated pupils from six schools; clustering by school not considered (p.61); not a unit-of-analysis error.
integrity_note: (1) Sample 44 (Abstract, p.61) vs 22 in Table 1. (2) Treatment post-test rose 15.17 to 48.18 (control 11.50 to 16.60); with higher = more aggression this indicates worsening, yet authors conclude CBI reduced aggression. (3) Table 1 df '1.25', F 2.78, sig .00, partial eta2 .99 - internally impossible. (4) Means incompatible with 29-item scale scoring and inclusion cut-off (cluster mean 2.50).
reconciliation_notes: Domains differing: D1 (A1 Some concerns, A2 High; final Some concerns: Individual allocation by coin toss is a stated random method (p.62), so the contradictory 'non-randomized ... non-equivalent' label (p.61) does not reduce it to an unsupported claim; concerns remain (pupils tossed coins themselves knowing which face meant treatment, so no concealment; exactly 11 vs 11; pretest 11.50 vs 15.17, SD 3.09/6.98, compatible with chance at n = 11 per arm; Table 1): Some concerns. Overall unchanged (High via D3).) Overall High by RoB 2 rule (D3 High); both assessors agreed on overall.

outcome_assessed: Bullying behaviour (Bullying Behaviour Observatory Scale, researcher-developed, 25 items; higher = more bullying); post-test after the treatment period; REBT vs no treatment (Tables 1, 3)
support_D1: Abstract: 'Simple random sampling technique was used to assign groups into two as experimental and control groups'; Methodology: 'non-equivalent control group design' with two co-educational schools selected by simple random sampling and no allocation procedure or concealment described (Abstract; Methodology). Allocation called random but unsupported and contradictory: rated High per guide. Baseline similar (77.95 vs 78.26; Table 1).
support_D1b: Bullies identified with the BBOS (Abstract; Methodology); timing of identification relative to group assignment not reported, and recruiters' knowledge of allocation unknown.
support_D2: No-treatment control; pupils and therapist aware of allocation; treatment length given as 5 weeks (Abstract) and 6 weeks (Methodology); no fidelity or attendance data.
support_D3: 109 allocated (53 + 56) and 109 analysed (Table 1; Table 3 total df).
support_D4: Researcher-developed 'observatory' scale 'checked by the researchers through observation' (Methodology); who rated (pupil, teacher or researcher) is not stated, and raters were not reported to be blinded; items reshuffled at post-test only to limit recall.
support_D5: No protocol or registration; single outcome; ANCOVA table reports Group F=129.46 with decision 'NS' and sig 0.003 while text claims significance, and Sex sig printed as 3.140 (Table 3); internal inconsistency but no evidence of selection among multiple outcomes or analyses.
unit_of_analysis_note: Two schools (likely one per arm); pupil-level ANCOVA, clustering ignored (Methodology; Table 3).
integrity_note: (1) Abstract vs Methodology conflicts: population 2000 SS3 vs 2,368 SS11 in 12 schools; treatment 5 vs 6 weeks; random assignment vs non-equivalent design. (2) Control pretest 78.26 to posttest 80.08 (an increase) reported as 'Mean Gain 1.82' (Table 1). (3) Table 2 REBT gender means 15.56/15.43 inconsistent with REBT post-test mean 33.26 (Tables 1-2). (4) Table 3 decisions and significance values inconsistent (Group 'NS' p 0.003; Sex sig 3.140).
reconciliation_notes: Tool differed (A1 RoB 2 cluster, A2 ROBINS-I V2; final RoB 2 cluster: Abstract: 'Simple random sampling technique was used to assign groups into two as experimental and control groups', while Methodology describes a 'quasi-experimental ... non-equivalent control group design' with two schools. Guide rule for random-claimed, unsupported, contradictory allocation: RoB 2 cluster with D1 High (as R2762).) Because of the tool difference every domain and the overall differed; final domain ratings follow assessor 1 after re-reading the full text (D1 High; D1b Some concerns; D2 Some concerns; D3 Low; D4 Some concerns; D5 Some concerns). Overall High by RoB 2 rule (D1 High); assessors' overall judgements differed only by tool (High vs Serious).

outcome_assessed: Examination cheating behaviour (researcher-developed self-report Examination Cheating Behavior Scale, ECBS, 20 items, range 20-80, higher = more cheating); post-test at end of the 4-week (8-session) intervention; REBT vs conventional counselling. Only outcome reported; no mental health scale (Tables 3-5)
support_D1: Contradictory allocation description, so RoB 2 used with D1 High per guide. Abstract and Design section call it a quasi-experimental pre-test post-test non-equivalent control group design and state 'randomization is not possible since the students are in intact classes' (Materials and Methods, Design, p.507). Yet Participants (p.508) and Experimental Procedures (p.511) say the two intact classes 'were randomly assigned'; no method of sequence generation or concealment is given. Schools chosen by purposive sampling; one class per arm (2 clusters). Pretest means similar (REBT 65.21 SD 6.43 vs CC 62.69 SD 6.70, Table 3/4) but with one cluster per arm school, class and therapist are fully confounded with arm.
support_D1b: Whole intact classes appear to have been used (Participants, p.508), which limits scope for selective recruitment, but the report does not state when pupils were identified or consented relative to allocation, or whether all class members took part; allocation and rapport visit occurred in week 2 before the pretest (Experimental Procedures, p.511). Arm sizes unequal (28 vs 39).
support_D2: Pupils and therapists aware of allocation (different interventions delivered by different therapists: REBT by an educational psychologist, CC by a counsellor; Therapists, p.509). Treatment integrity monitored by an assessor recording attendance (Treatment Integrity, p.508; Experimental Procedures, p.511, 'fully administered and followed'). No deviations reported; analysis appears to include all 67 by assigned group (Table 5, corrected total df 66). Some concerns because no information on attendance results or deviations and lack of blinding in a behavioural intervention.
support_D3: Sample of 67 (28 REBT, 39 CC) stated in Participants (p.508) and Table 3; Table 4 gives N = 28 and 39 at both pre- and post-test; Table 7 cell ns sum to 28 (16+12) and 39 (19+20); ANCOVA corrected total df 66 (Table 5), so all 67 allocated pupils were analysed. No attrition or exclusions reported; no flow diagram. Text 'n = 28' for CC post-test (Results, p.514) contradicts the pretest n = 39 in the same sentence and all tables, so treated as a typo (recorded in integrity_note).
support_D4: Outcome is self-reported examination cheating by unblinded pupils who received a psychological intervention whose content stresses that cheating is harmful and irrational (Treatment Manual, p.509; Table 1), so social desirability responding may differ by arm. Scale developed by the researchers; validity limited to expert review and alpha 0.86 in 25 pupils (Measures, p.508). Post-test administered by the research assistants who delivered the interventions (Experimental Procedures, p.511).
support_D5: No protocol or trial registration mentioned. Single outcome scale and the analysis (ANCOVA with pretest covariate) are described in Data Analysis (p.511) and results reported for all three stated hypotheses (Introduction, p.507; Tables 4-7), so no clear evidence of selection, but no pre-specified plan available to check.
unit_of_analysis_note: Two intact classes from two schools (one cluster per arm) allocated; outcomes analysed at pupil level with ANCOVA (Table 5, error df 62) with no adjustment for clustering. Effective sample size is essentially two clusters; intervention effect is confounded with school and therapist. Requires design-effect adjustment (ICC imputation) or sensitivity analysis in the meta-analysis.
integrity_note: (1) Table 6 (male vs female) reports exactly the same values as Table 4 (REBT vs CC): pretest 65.21/6.43 vs 62.69/6.70, post-test 39.21/12.72 vs 55.36/8.95, mean gains 26.00 vs 7.33 (pp.513, 515), and pooling Table 7 cells for males gives post-test about 44.2 not 39.21, so Table 6 appears duplicated from Table 4. Table 4 and Table 7 are internally consistent for REBT (39.21) and CC (55.36). (2) Text gives CC post-test n = 28 vs Table 4 n = 39 (p.514). (3) Chi-square chi2(1) = 0.464 reported with p = 0.621 (expected about 0.50) (Table 3); Levene p = .070 reported as 'p > 0.50' (Assumption Check, p.512). (4) Pretest covariate not associated with post-test (F = 1.006, p = .320, partial eta2 .016, Table 5), implausible for a pre-post measure on the same scale. (5) Partial eta2 misinterpreted as '46.8% reduction' (p.514); therapists also described as 'research assistants' (p.509). Implausibly large effect for a four-week, eight-session school intervention (REBT male gain 37.56, post-test SD 3.28, Table 7; partial eta2 .468). Data said to be deposited at Science Data Bank (not checked). Large effect (adjusted means 41.05 vs 55.24) from two classes; flag for sensitivity analysis.
reconciliation_notes: Tool agreed (RoB 2 cluster; contradictory 'randomly assigned' vs 'randomization is not possible', so RoB 2 with D1 High per guide); only wording of tool label and outcome differed. D3 differed (x1 Some concerns; x2 Low): re-read Participants, Table 3, Table 4, Table 7 and Table 5; Ns of 28/39 are consistent across all tables and ANCOVA corrected total df 66 confirms 67 analysed = 67 allocated, the single 'n = 28' for CC post-test in the text is a typo, so final Low. All other domains agreed (D1 High, D1b, D2, D4, D5 Some concerns). Overall High agreed (D1 High).

outcome_assessed: Total bullying behavioural tendency (Adolescent Peer Relation Instrument, APRI, 18 items, 6-point, self-report; higher = more bullying); immediate post-test after 8 weeks; REBT vs placebo study-habit control (Table 1(b) p.301: control 53.93 vs REBT 31.67, n=30 each; no SDs)
support_D1: Methodology/Research Design p.299: participants 'assigned to two experimental groups by simple coin tossing'; Participants p.299: 'randomly assigned to REBT and control groups'; Procedure p.299 claims 'strict process of randomisation'. Random sequence stated, but no allocation concealment described, the same section labels the study 'quasi experimental', and 60 pupils were 'purposively selected from two co-educational schools' with counsellor help. Baseline 'statistically equivalent' is asserted (p.299) but no pre-test means/SDs or test reported. Hence RoB 2 with D1 Some concerns.
support_D2: Procedure (b) p.299-300: REBT 8 weekly 45-min sessions; control 'placebo training of study habit' described as one 45-min reading-skills session, so attention not matched. Pupils and deliverers could not be blinded; no information on adherence, contamination between arms (two schools, unclear whether arm was confounded with school) or deviations. Analysis appears by assigned group (Table 1(b) N=30/30, p.301) but ANCOVA df inconsistent. Some concerns.
support_D3: Table 1(b) p.301 reports N=30 control and N=30 REBT, matching the 60 enrolled (Participants p.299); no attrition reported, so outcome data appear complete for the primary comparison. Low (note Table 1(a) within df=59 is inconsistent with N=60, see integrity note).
support_D4: Instrumentation p.299: APRI self-report (6-point frequency scale, alpha 0.83-0.92) completed by pupils who knew they received REBT or study-habit sessions; Procedure (c) p.300 same APRI as post-test; no assessor blinding possible for self-report. Some concerns.
support_D5: No protocol or registration mentioned. Results p.300-301 give only F ratios and DMRT means for post-test (Table 1(a)-(b)) without SDs or pre-test data; unclear whether 53.93 vs 31.67 are adjusted or raw; abstract reports F(2,60)=9.345 inconsistent with two groups; ANCOVA/ANOVA choices for H1-H3 not prespecified. Some concerns.
unit_of_analysis_note: Individually allocated by coin toss, so no cluster adjustment needed; however REBT was presumably delivered in groups and pupils came from two schools (p.299) with no information on whether arms were balanced across schools, so school/therapist clustering is ignored. Treat as individually randomised.
integrity_note: Multiple internal inconsistencies (pp.297-301, from page images): (1) Table 1(a) ANCOVA lists Row df=2 for a two-group comparison, Column SS=Interaction SS=617.148, Within df=59 for N=60 (impossible after covariate/groups), and F=9.345 does not equal MS 2883.695/ (7001.686/59=118.67) =24.3. (2) Abstract F(2,60) and Discussion F(2,60) also inconsistent with two groups. (3) Tables 2(a) and 3(a) use between-group df=2 for two-level factors. (4) Subgroup means within REBT arm (male 35.01, female 32.59, N=15/15; JSS 40.77 N=12, SSS 46.83 N=18) cannot average to the REBT arm mean 31.67 (Table 1(b)); JSS/SSS weighted mean about 44.4. (5) Abstract says 30 males/30 females and 30 JSS/30 SSS overall, but REBT-only subgroup N do not match class split (12/18). (6) Text says age 'eleven (11) and nineteen (17)'. (7) Discussion refers to 'Reality Therapy group' and 'HIV-risk behaviour', apparently copied from another study. (8) Tables 2(a) and 3(a) analyse the same 30 REBT pupils yet give different corrected total SS (1066.705 vs 1112.595), and Table 2(a) F=15.956 is not reproducible from the means (2.42-point difference, n 15/15, error MS 18.107 gives F about 2.4). (9) Published in Nigerian Journal of Parasitology, an off-topic venue. Effect data are unreliable; consider excluding from meta-analysis or sensitivity analysis only.
reconciliation_notes: Assessors agreed on tool (RoB 2, individually randomised; x2 labelled 'RoB 2 (individually randomised)', standardised to 'RoB 2') and on every domain: D1 Some concerns, D2 Some concerns, D3 Low, D4 Some concerns, D5 Some concerns, overall High. Verified against page images pp.299-301: coin-toss allocation of individual pupils with 'strict process of randomisation' but labelled 'quasi experimental' and purposive selection, no concealment and no baseline data (p.299); placebo was one 45-min study-habit session vs eight 45-min REBT sessions (pp.299-300); Table 1(b) n 30/30 equals the 60 enrolled. Overall High because four domains are Some concerns and the reported analysis is not reproducible, which substantially lowers confidence. x1 support text kept; integrity_note merged from both (x2 added the non-reproducible Table 2(a) F; reconciler added differing total SS for the same REBT arm in Tables 2(a)/3(a)).
